text: Rickets is characterized by inadequate mineralization of the growth plates and bone matrix of the skeleton and represents a heterogeneous group of disorders with both acquired and inherited subtypes. Patients with rickets typically present with decreased serum calcium and/or phosphorus levels [ 1 ]. In addition to various skeletal deformities, hypocalcemia-related symptoms, such as tetany, convulsions, laryngospasm, and muscle weakness, may also be observed [ 2 ]. Although nutritional rickets, caused by insufficient intake of vitamin D or calcium, is the most commonly encountered subtype, recognition of inherited forms, including hypophosphatemic and vitamin D-dependent rickets, is increasing due to advances in molecular genetic diagnostic techniques [ 3 ].
